description: Content evals for the chaos-vector-catalogue skill. Each scenario runs the same prompt twice -- once with the skill loaded, once without -- to measure the value delta. If with-skill and without-skill outputs are indistinguishable, the skill is not adding value; redesign or delete.

scenarios.prompt: Pick a chaos vector for apm.yml schema and write a regression-trap test that asserts a graceful error message when the file lists a non-existent target.
with_skill_expected: Loads references/apm_yml_schema.md only (not all six surfaces).
Uses tests/chaos/_harness.run_apm to invoke the real binary (subprocess), not a Python-level YAML parser.
Captures actual exit code and stderr, not asserted ones.
Test file lives under tests/chaos/ and is decorated with @pytest.mark.chaos.
Test asserts exit code != 0 AND a specific stderr fragment, classified as 'graceful'.
Test name encodes the vector signature (so memory/chaos-monkey/findings.md can dedupe).
without_skill_likely: Writes a unit test that parses YAML at the Python level, bypassing the CLI surface.
Asserts an exception class instead of a process-level exit code + stderr.
Places the test under tests/unit/ without the chaos marker.
No vector signature recorded; future runs re-discover the same finding.
scenarios.pass_criteria: with_skill output captures real subprocess evidence under tests/chaos/ with the chaos marker; without_skill output does not.

scenarios.prompt: Look at past chaos findings in memory and pick a vector that has NOT been hardened yet for the auth-flows surface.
with_skill_expected: Reads memory/chaos-monkey/findings.md before proposing a vector.
Returns a vector signature that is NOT present in the memory file.
States explicit ruling-out of any candidate already in memory.
without_skill_likely: Re-proposes a previously hardened vector (no memory awareness).
Skips memory entirely and improvises from generic auth-failure intuition.
scenarios.pass_criteria: with_skill names memory/chaos-monkey/findings.md by path AND its proposed signature does not collide with any entry; without_skill does not consult memory.

scenarios.prompt: Reproduce: invoke apm install with a lockfile that is deleted mid-run. Classify the outcome and write the regression-trap test.
with_skill_expected: Calls run_apm (subprocess) and captures real exit code, stderr, stdout, timed_out flag.
Classifies the outcome as exactly one of: graceful, silent, uncontrolled, using the classification table in SKILL.md.
Cites the captured evidence (exit code value, stderr fragment, state-mutation observation) as the basis for the classification, not LLM intuition.
Emits an issue body using the inline template (vector signature + classification + reproduction commands + recommended hardening).
Does NOT fix the bug; explicitly states the hard-constraint boundary.
without_skill_likely: Classifies without captured evidence (LLM asserts 'this is uncontrolled' from prose).
Proposes a code fix in src/apm_cli/ alongside the test (violates the hard-constraint boundary).
Skips the timed_out check and confuses a hang with a silent failure.
scenarios.pass_criteria: with_skill cites real subprocess evidence to justify the classification AND does not propose source changes; without_skill either lacks evidence or crosses the boundary.

ship_gate: On at least 2 of 3 scenarios, with_skill output meets pass_criteria and without_skill output does not. If 0 or 1 scenarios show a delta, redesign or delete the skill.
